subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Agent core is an append-only JSONL ledger: scoped idempotency keys, CAS replacement, content-addressed payloads, enforced event chains
evidence: src/ledger/ledger.ts:323-328 (idempotency scope + conflicting-reuse reject), src/domain/events.ts, test/unit/ledger.test.ts:103,119,213,491 (replay-as-no-op, key-reuse reject, withdrawal CAS, requested->admitted->started chain)
one_why: Crash-resume, fork lineage (ledger.ts:488-495 enforces exactly one run.forked), and audit stop being bolted on - every loop mechanism (compaction, approval, budget charge) is a validated event, which is why test names read as invariants instead of behaviors; heavier lift than any anchor attempted.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Teto: a second cognitive lane that observes only completed owner steps and may interrupt via A2A only when advice could change the next decision
evidence: src/runtime/teto-lane-scheduler.ts:100, src/runtime/run-runtime.ts:537-545 (TetoScheduler/IntentNavigator wiring), docs/runtime-loop-baseline.md:16 (one inference per released batch), CHANGELOG.md:24-26
one_why: Closest corpus analog is codex's guardian pool, but Teto is a continuous per-lane observer with its own context, start/stop authority for the owner, and explicit silence-by-default - a distinct multi-agent primitive, though causal value is still self-claimed pending the arm in nausicaa-harness-3.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Feature shipped with a preregistered experiment: frozen fixture+scorer hashes, four arms including a shadow placebo, per-pair budget envelopes, 95% bootstrap
evidence: test/eval/preregistered-contract.ts:13-27 (CONTROL_ARM teto-shadow, PREREGISTERED_ARMS), :32-57 (BudgetEnvelope, ArmPlan), test/eval/runner.ts, test/eval/teto-live-restraint.ts
one_why: No other subject measures its own flagship feature against a placebo arm with a hash-frozen contract written before the live runs; if the field adopts any causal-eval methodology, copy this shape - the arms are offline-verifiable (preregistered-contract.test.ts) even though live runs need credentials.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Prompt-cache performance is an observed ledger projection and a release gate: recorded live probe artifact with provenance yields pass/hold on shipping
evidence: src/observability/cache-evidence.ts:11-33 (prefixContinuity, providerCache per attempt), test/eval/cache-artifact.ts:21,38-59 (CACHE_PROBE_TASK_ID, releaseDecision pass|hold, evidenceDigest)
one_why: Anchors warm or mark caches (pi, claw-code's broken detector); nobody else ties cache behavior to a release decision or derives prefix continuity from the event journal instead of an in-process counter - and the projection deliberately excludes prompt fingerprints so it is UI-safe.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Two compaction tiers: per-turn selection plus a deterministic pressure gate with predicted-gain floor, contiguous group retention, and output-headroom re-check
evidence: src/runtime/main-loop.ts:668-684 (selectCompaction), :827-870 (compactForPressure adopted only if headroom >= 1 token), src/fukai/compaction-pressure.ts:9-16,53-75 (minimumGainTokens, insufficient-predicted-gain), test/unit/fukai-compaction-pressure.test.ts
one_why: The pressure decision needs no provider call and can say no (skip when predicted gain is below floor), and a candidate summary competes against the live reservation before adoption - avoids the wasted-compact-and-overflow cycle every tier-1 harness hits; closest existing implementations are codex's token-budget tier, so reuse the decision function shape.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Context budget overflow degrades in fixed steps - drop compaction, then drop skill catalog and its paired schema atomically - never fails the turn
evidence: src/runtime/main-loop.ts:742-749 (FukaiBudgetError -> rebuild without compaction), :753-764 (drop skill tool + catalog together and retry), :759-770 (hide schema when catalog not rendered), src/fukai/context-provider.ts:133-136
one_why: The invariant 'an optimization never displaces required context' plus schema/capital coherence (a tool is never advertised for context the provider elided) is a generalizable budget pattern; most subjects either fail-open with truncated required content or crash the turn.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Skill discovery returns immutable metadata-only snapshots; bodies load only on explicit invocation, with changed-during-load rejection
evidence: src/mowe/edges/skills.ts:257-260 (discoverSkills doc), :366-411 (loadSkill with TOCTOU checks :391-403), src/fukai/context-provider.ts:60-62 (bounded catalog: 128 items, 64KB total)
one_why: Converges with the seeded pattern (cline/pi-style catalogs) but adds a per-path sourceId + turn-snapshot generation model so in-flight turns keep the catalog they were built against - the catalog-eviction-vs-in-flight-request race other subjects leave unsolved.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: workspace profile: probed-then-used OS confinement (seatbelt/bwrap) that fails closed by removing the bash tool, hiding secret dirs; default profile remains full-access
evidence: src/tools/workspace-command-sandbox.ts:167-207 (probe never runs the command), :129-134,159-161 (unavailable -> throw), :32-38 (.aws/.ssh/.gnupg/.kube/.nausicaa protected), src/runtime/run-runtime.ts:471-484 (shell enabled only if availability().available), README.md:262, test/unit/workspace-command-sandbox.test.ts:90,163
one_why: Exact inverse of nanocoder's fail-open jail: probe failure means the capability does not exist, and profile refusal is surfaced as unavailable rather than as a command error; the honest caveat is that nothing under the default full-access profile binds - security-posture honesty per SECURITY.md:3-5 keeps it nuance, not safety-hole.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Runs are owned through TTL leases with monotonic fencing tokens; daemon workers persist hash-chained recovery journals and durable writes re-check the lease
evidence: src/runtime/execution-lease.ts:9-15,53-58 (fencingToken, clock-regressed states), src/runtime/file-execution-lease.ts:225 (fence checked under file lock), src/runtime/daemon-worker-recovery-journal.ts:15-37 (uncertain/interrupted statuses, fingerprint-not-payload), src/runtime/session-controller.ts:512-517 (assertExecutionLease durable-write guard)
one_why: Distributed-systems ownership discipline imported into a coding harness: a zombie second instance cannot double-execute because appends fail the fence check - test/protocol/daemon-ledger-fence.test.ts proves it; only codex's daemon comes close, and no other TS subject has fencing at all.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Whole protocol plane tested offline against scripted ports: 20+ daemon/protocol specs, recovery suites, abort-parity tests; live provider suites excluded from npm test and CI
evidence: package.json:61 (--exclude test/live/** test/eval/** test/smoke/**), test/protocol/daemon-worker-recovery.test.ts, test/protocol/agent-loop-abort-parity.test.ts, test/recovery/, test/live/openrouter*.test.ts (credential-gated)
one_why: The seam design (ModelPort/Clock/every dep injectable) makes the daemon restart, fence-loss, and cancellation semantics deterministic to test - the abort-parity test between interactive and one-shot paths is the kind of cross-surface invariant property anchor codex has and pi/cline lack equivalents for.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: session-controller.ts at 6,365 LOC fuses host wiring, permission-mode mutation, model selection, polling, and TUI snapshotting despite the loop itself being separated
one_why: Per the errata the >5k product-surface docking factor applies here even though MainLoop is clean - the 8->9 architecture gap is 'loop/state separated from every product surface', and the session host is where policy, selection, and host coordination reconverge; if this one file is decomposed, architecture joins verification at 8.

subject: nausicaa-harness
title: Every adapted third-party snippet is attributed by upstream commit hash with an explicit not-copied boundary list
evidence: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES:3-5 (pi responsibilities named), :7-13 (Prime Agent commit 7787f074, what was and was not ported), :35-38 (Prime daemon/RPC/IPython explicitly not copied), src/tools/workspace-command-sandbox.ts:94-98 (DeepSeek sandbox-local commit aa6c361a; Codex boundary credited)
one_why: The audit trail synthesis needs for provenance is volunteered by the subject itself - a cheap norm (commit pin + adopted-boundary paragraph per ported file) that would resolve most fork-detection ambiguity in this corpus; MIT compliance intact throughout, no license-risk finding.
